They never say \\u0022Review pull request\\u0022. Its acceptance criterion is that the drafted reply is walked with walk-pr-review-findings and posted only on the owner\\u0027s go.\u0022,\u0022A mention on a pull request someone else wrote, and a mention on a pull request an own live task already covers, behave exactly as they do today (full-review mint, and attach plus the existing follow-up gates).\u0022,\u0022\\u0060ObservedReviewMention\\u0060 and the daemon\\u0027s \\u0022observed a mention\\u0022 log line record the answer-only mint as its own outcome, so \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 and the log show which shape ran.\u0022,\u0022Unit tests over the decision, with no database, no branch, and no GitHub: own pull request leads to the answer-only mint; someone else\\u0027s pull request leads to today\\u0027s mint; an own covering task leads to today\\u0027s attach. The pull request\\u0027s author is matched by GitHub account id where GitHub reports one, and falls back to a case-insensitive login comparison only when it does not.\u0022,\u0022\\u0060docs/operations.md\\u0060\\u0027s mention row and the Decisions Log say that a mention on your own pull request gets an answer lap, never a review of your own work, and why: the review-request trigger can never reach the author, and the author already holds the context the 2f079bcd ruling wanted the review to supply.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Read the mentioning comment before anything is claimed: who wrote it, who it tags, and whether it asks anything of this install\\u0027s owner.
